data.title: Stop Cut holes tunnelling out at spike valleys

fields.actions: Cut's hole depth was the deepest point where any part of the opening reaches the cavity. On steep spikes part of each opening reaches it only through the next spike's wall, 20+ mm down; cutting that deep came out through the neighbour at the valley (with Break out: one extra hole per valley), and without Break out the face failed as 'too thick'. solid/shell.js now caps each ray without piercing and opens as deep as that cap leaves room for: deeper entries keep a floor, the face must at least open through its own wall. Faces that must still break out cut as shallow as opens them, a quarter wall past the entry. Builds that worked without Break out are unchanged.
fields.verify: npm test (through.test.js 'opens through each face's own wall rather than tunnelling out through a neighbour'); bash scripts/acceptance.sh

data.title: Fix float32 crossings in Cut + rounding output

fields.actions: Cut + rounding builds had self-intersections only once positions were rounded to float32 for the STL. Cause: near-flat triangles in the boolean output (a corner 1e-7..1e-4 mm from the opposite edge, mostly along the rim crease where a hole meets a rounding strip, sometimes a fan over several corners on one line). solid/csg.js fixFlat now removes every triangle flatter than 1e-5 x the part size: flipped with its neighbour across the long edge when neither result is flat, otherwise the middle corner slides along the line onto the nearer end of the edge, only where every surrounding triangle stays within tolerance of its plane, keeps its orientation, and a flat one stays flat. One vertex-to-triangle index is built once (no Map keyed on u*nV+v), so build time is unchanged.
fields.verify: npm test (through.test.js 'has no crossings once positions are rounded to float32 for the STL'); bash scripts/acceptance.sh

The 4 left in the broad sweep are jittered globes/twisted globes with rounding whose crossings also appear with Straight sides or closed (Stage-2 rounding, card f83117b2). Tried manifold simplify(1e-5..1e-4 x size) and snapping to float32 first: no gain over fixFlat alone, 1e-4 made it worse. data.title: Add opening sides: Tapered, Straight and Cut

fields.actions: Form → Openings → Sides (state key openingAxis: center | normal | through). Tapered keeps the origin-ray construction, byte-identical to before. data.title: Stop Cut + rounding leaving rods inside spikes

fields.actions: Under Cut the closed shell's cavity was a copy of the rounded outside, so its spike ridges and tips were rounded with the full radius. That material lies inside what the depth probe treats as cavity; the cutters trimmed it into thin rods across the windows (extra genus) and, at small radii, loose specks (an icosahedron at Spike 2.38 with 0.6 mm rounding came out as 10 bodies). When no edge radius exceeds the wall, Cut now builds the cavity as the sharp inner polyhedron (solid/shell.js sharpInner), which is the surface one wall inside a ridge rounded by r <= wall. Larger radii keep the copied cavity; no rods appeared there in sweeps. Tapered and Straight are unchanged.
fields.verify: npm test (through.test.js 'leaves no rods or loose bits inside rounded spikes'); bash scripts/acceptance.sh

data.title: Fix rounding on subdivided and smoothed meshes

fields.actions: Review the Smooth × Rounding math on subdivided meshes and fix the shell-stage breakage. Findings: (1) Stage-2 face rings carried only two points per internal seam, so subdivided faces had 3–7-ray openings — fillets became bare triangles/chords, volume rose with rounding; (2) Smooth turns every sub-facet crease into a dihedral, and at low Smooth the rolling-ball strips are micrometres wide — their caps collapse to zero area in float32 and compile throws. Fix in src/solid/edgeround.js: lengthwise sampling along internal seams (shared per seam), a scale-relative strip-width floor (1e-3·R) so shallow creases stay sharp, one merge tolerance for strip ends/corner points, flat wedge caps for pinched corners and corners with sharp spokes, a mitre ribbon for knees (parent edge bent at a subdivision midpoint), and reuse of the strip end when a macro boundary runs straight through a corner.

data.title: Round the parent macro graph under Smooth instead of its facets

fields.actions: Smooth (skeleton-stage rolling-ball projection) and Rounding (shell-stage strips) implement the same fillet twice; Stage-2 currently fillets every sub-facet crease Smooth leaves. Unite facets by parent tag in solid/macro-topo.js regardless of coplanarity, so Rounding follows only parent dihedrals, and generalize the knee ribbon in solid/edgeround.js into a proper mitre for bent macro edges. Also consider the Stage-1 rim-arc direction (toward the origin, not the face normal), which skews rim roundovers on off-axis micro faces.
